learning_outcomes.text: Understand the key concepts related to relational databases and database management systems.
Have a thorough understanding of SQL and relational algebra and know how to use these languages to extract information of interest.
Understand the principles underlying database design and the Entity-Relationship conceptual model, and how schemas expressed in this model can be represented in various relational forms.
Be able to recognize and enforce data constraints of arbitrary complexity and manage data access through authorization.
Understand the problems associated with concurrent transaction execution and how to avoid them.

syllabus_topics: Database Management Systems (DBMSs) Information Systems and the role of DBMSs
Basic functionalities of DBMSs: 3-tier architecture, languages, access and concurrency control, fault tolerance
The Relational Data Model Basic concepts: domains, attributes, tuples and relations, 1NF relations, null values
Data constraints: on domains, tuples, keys, referential integrity
The Relational Algebra Unary operators: selection, projection, and renaming
Binary operators: natural join, union, and difference
Derived operators: intersection, theta-join, and division
Algebra with null values: 3-valued logic, outer join
The SQL (Structured Query Language) Language Data definition language (DDL) and definition of constraints
Definition of views and recursive queries
Granting and revoking authorities and privileges
The Entity-Relationship (E/R) Model Basic elements: entities, relationships, attributes
Conceptual Design (hints) Collecting and analyzing requirements
Logical Design Mapping entities and relationships onto relational tables
Restructuring an E/R schema: dropping hierarchies, managing multi-valued attributes, choosing the principal identifiers
Optimization criteria: Workloads (data volumes and navigation schemas), redundancy analysis, partitioning and merging entities and relationships
Normalization of Relational Schemas Functional dependencies and data anomalies
teaching_methods: Classroom exercises led by the instructor
Practical laboratory exercises using specific software tools (DBMS client and a design tool)
assessment_rules: The exam consists of a laboratory test covering the entire course program, including several exercises with fixed scores and multiple-choice questions. The score is based on a 20-point scale, converted to a 33-point scale. A minimum score of 3 points on the first two exercises (out of 8 total points) and at least one correctly answered multiple-choice question are required to pass. The grade earned in a test is valid indefinitely, but taking a new test voids any previously earned grade. The use of personal laptops, tablets, smartphones, or AI tools is prohibited.
